r_eff_band.caveat: Two 181.8 kohm bleed strings in parallel give 90.9 kohm, not 45.45 kohm, so R1's 4560.74 ohm is definitively REJECTED. However the review's 4801.65043 ohm cannot be reproduced from exact ideal resistors: with RLOAD 5200 || bleed 90900 || (100k + 100k + 1900.6) = 4475.91 ohm. The two differ by ~7.3 % of a sub-ohm design choice in the divider tail group, which is a hand-computation artefact rather than a physical effect. Every load-dependent quantity in this matrix is therefore quoted over the 4475.9-4801.7 ohm band, and no conclusion here depends on the difference.
r_eff_band.verdict: R_eff corrected to the 4475.9-4801.7 ohm band; 4560.74 ohm rejected and used nowhere.

resistor_reference.description: The CURRENT unchanged fixture: one 5200 ohm resistor to ground plus two 181.8 kohm bleeder strings plus the LT3757A feedback divider.
resistor_reference.note: This is the ONLY load model that has ever been simulated. It is a reference, not the real load.

small_signal_statement: A resistor presents +R at the output node. A const-power sink presents -R = -V^2/P. For this R_eff the resistor damping term and the const-power term have OPPOSITE sign, so the output pole migrates and the stability question becomes a DIFFERENT question. Any stability statement derived from the resistor fixture does NOT transfer to P2 and must never be presented as if it did.
